edition.locus: Eusebius HE 5.1.5-6 (the onset of the persecution)

source_text: Τὸ μὲν οὖν μέγεθος τῆς ἐνθάδε θλίψεως καὶ τὴν τοσαύτην τῶν ἐθνῶν εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους ὀργὴν καὶ ὅσα ὑπέμειναν οἱ μακάριοι μάρτυρες, ἐπ᾽ ἀκριβὲς οὔθ᾽ ἡμεῖς εἰπεῖν ἱκανοὶ οὔτε μὴν γραφῇ περιληφθῆναι δυνατόν. Παντὶ γὰρ σθένει ἐνέσκηψεν ὁ ἀντικείμενος, προοιμιαζόμενος ἤδη τὴν ἀδεῶς μέλλουσαν ἔσεσθαι παρουσίαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ διὰ πάντων διῆλθεν, ἐθίζων τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ καὶ προγυμνάζων κατὰ τῶν δούλων τοῦ θεοῦ, ὥστε μὴ μόνον οἰκιῶν καὶ βαλανείων καὶ ἀγορᾶς εἴργεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ καθόλου φαίνεσθαί ἡμῶν τινα αὐτοῖς ἀπειρῆσθαι ἐν ὁποίῳ δήποτε τόπῳ.
pass_a_gloss: Now the magnitude of the affliction here and the so-great anger of the peoples against the saints and how many things the blessed witnesses endured, neither are we competent to say exactly nor indeed is it possible to be comprised in writing. For with all strength the opposer burst in, making a prelude already to his coming that is about to be without fear, and he went through all things, habituating his own people and pre-training them against the slaves of God, so that not only from houses and baths and marketplace to be shut off, but also in general for any one of us to appear before them to have been forbidden in whatever place at all.
pass_b_english: The greatness of the suffering here, the immense fury of the pagans against the holy ones, and all that the blessed martyrs endured — we are not equal to telling it exactly, nor could it be embraced in writing. For the Adversary broke in with all his might, offering even now a prelude to his own coming that is to be fearless, and he left nothing untried, habituating his own people and drilling them beforehand against the servants of God, so that we were barred not only from houses and baths and marketplace, but it was forbidden for any of us to show ourselves before them at all, in any place whatever.

choices.why: articular substantive participle marks a single known hostile agent acting with all his force and prefiguring his own coming, not merely human opponents in context
genitive plural in contrast to τοὺς ἁγίους and τοὺς δούλους τοῦ θεοῦ denotes unbelieving outsiders directing anger against Christians here, not Israel-versus-nations

choices.english: his coming that is to be fearless
choices.why: adverb ἀδεῶς modifies the future participial idea of his coming, describing its unrestrained character, not the manner of the present prelude
